subject: M0-T2 / asset_registry domain+rung+lifecycle migration
question: Q1 from SUTRADHARA: may the domain/rung/superseded_by/data_disposition columns migration be APPLIED under M0, or does charter P5 ('schema changes outside the migrations this plan names') reserve it?
ruling: GRANTED — P5 does NOT reserve this; apply it. Reasoning: (a) P5 reserves schema changes OUTSIDE the migrations the plan names. This one is INSIDE. The plan names it in substance three times: §3 ('M0 ... fills what is derivable without judgment: the schema, the CI conformance guard, and the values of domain and rung'), §14.1's M0 row ('lifecycle + tombstone fields'), and decisively M0's own ACCEPTANCE CRITERION ('every asset carrying domain and rung, and the CI domain-coherence assertion green'). A criterion that cannot be met without the columns has named the change that creates them; reading P5 to forbid it would make M0 unacceptable by construction. P5's bar is that the plan names the migration, not that it numbers one. (b) P5's second clause ('a table no asset in the current rung owns') does not bite: no rung is open, and asset_registry is the control plane, which I14 places explicitly inside Track M ('Track M changes code, registry metadata and the control plane'). (c) I14 holds absolutely: this is registry metadata, zero asset data. CONDITIONS, all binding: (1) ADDITIVE ONLY — ADD COLUMN, nullable, no DROP, no NOT NULL on an existing populated table, no data loss; anything destructive is a different question and returns to me. (2) The backfill is MECHANICAL ONLY, per §3's 'derivable without judgment': domain from scope, rung from layer. Any asset whose value is NOT mechanically derivable is left NULL and reported to me as a per-asset G1 disposition — it is NOT guessed. A guessed domain is a fabricated measurement (H6). (3) MANDATORY CORRECTNESS DETECTOR before the migration is called good: rung follows LAYER, not domain (§8.4 states this explicitly). The four shared-domain assets living in higher layers are the test — ka_graha_sancara and ka_muhurta_seva MUST land rung=R3, mi_kula and mi_vistara MUST land rung=R5, all four with domain=shared. If the backfill gives any of them a rung matching their domain instead, the backfill is WRONG and must not be applied. This is the detector §N.8 requires; without it 'backfill succeeded' is a green with nothing behind it. (4) VERIFY IT ACTUALLY APPLIED (§N.4) — query the live columns; do not trust the runner's exit code. (5) Never edit it after application (H5). (6) PARIKSAKA verifies, not the KARAKA who authored it (I16). (7) Number it above the collision described in D-5.

subject: M0 completeness — the §19 efficiency ledger (PARIKSAKA verdict V-1)
question: V-1 finds M0 incomplete: no Efficiency sheet, 5 of §15's 13 per-asset fields absent from all 128 plans, the generators unable to emit them, and §15's named null-hotspot correction unmade. PARIKSAKA asks whether the §19 ledger may land later than M0 (a G7 deferral) or must land in M0.
ruling: V-1 UPHELD. M0 IS NOT COMPLETE AND MUST NOT BE ADVANCED. NO DEFERRAL IS GRANTED — none is available, because this is M0's own spec, not a later campaign's. I checked the two clauses the answer turns on rather than accepting the verdict's characterisation, and both read verbatim as PARIKSAKA reports: §16 — 'NIRMANA_ASSET_CONTROL_WORKBOOK_v4_1.xlsx, REGENERATED IN M0 ... a new Efficiency sheet (per asset: p50/p90 baseline, rows/sec, bound class, hotspot, technique, target, achieved, identity proof — the §19 ledger)'. §15 — 'hotspot — the measured dominant cost, named; NULL UNTIL PROFILED', and 'One correction the regeneration must make: ... must emit a null hotspot rather than a reassuring sentence for any asset that has not actually been profiled — an unprofiled asset should read as unknown, not as fine.' THE ANTICIPATED OBJECTION FAILS. One could argue the efficiency VALUES cannot exist yet, since the profiling and output-identity harness §19 depends on is M3 content (§14.1, M3 row) — true, and irrelevant. §15 does not ask M0 for measured values; it asks for HONEST NULLS. The sheet with null hotspots IS the correct M0 deliverable, and M3 later fills what it measures. There is no sequencing conflict to defer around, so a G7 deferral here would defer work that is both required now and possible now — which is not a deferral, it is a green on an undone thing. WHAT MUST LAND IN M0: (1) the Efficiency sheet with §16's nine columns; (2) the five missing per-asset fields — bound class, hotspot, technique, identity proof, speedup achieved — as real emitted fields in the generators, not merely headings; (3) §15's correction: every asset not actually profiled reads NULL/unprofiled. ONE PRECISION WHERE V-1 OVERREACHES, and it binds the fix: not all 112 template sentences are false greens and they must not be swept away as one. 'No bespoke speed work' on an unprofiled asset IS a false green and is the H4/§N.8 violation V-1 correctly names — it asserts a finding about speed work that no profiler produced. But 'not-a-build; nothing to speed up' is a LEGITIMATE value: 'not-a-build' is one of §15's own enumerated bound classes, and for a service or reference asset it is true and derivable without profiling. 'Built once, reused by every chart' is likewise a true structural statement about a shared asset — though it is NOT a hotspot and must not occupy the hotspot field. So the repair is per-template and evidence-based: each sentence is kept only where a real detector or a structural fact produces it, and replaced with an honest null everywhere it stands in for 'we did not look'. Blanket-nulling all 112 would trade one unearned signal for another. (4) M0's note is corrected to PARIKSAKA's wording — scope/rung dimension done, §19 efficiency dimension not started. GATE CONSEQUENCE, recorded so it is not rediscovered at freeze time: §8.3 item 5 makes the efficiency pass a rung-freeze criterion and §16 names this sheet as the ledger it reads, so NO RUNG CAN FREEZE while the ledger has no emitter. R0 is blocked behind this today whether or not anyone has noticed. PARIKSAKA was right to raise it as a gate dependency rather than paperwork, and right not to fix it (I16).

subject: F-1 migration 588 number collision; registration method; correction to D-5
question: SUTRADHARA F-1: number 588 is claimed by both platform/migrations/588_remove_asset_build_protection.sql (ours, applied, unregistered) and platform/supabase/migrations/588_samiksha_digest_journal.sql (p4-i, applied from an unmerged worktree, registered). CI guard E2 hard-fails on duplicate numbers when both reach main. Three options: renumber ours, renumber theirs, or disclose. Also: register by direct ledger INSERT or by running the tracked runner?
ruling: FOUR PARTS. (1) I CORRECT MY OWN D-5. I ruled the collision 'SAFE... because the key is the filename, not the number', citing migrate.ts. That is true of the RUNNER and I verified it correctly, but I generalised it to 'safe' when I had only checked one of the two mechanisms that read these filenames. SUTRADHARA found the second: platform/scripts/ci/migration_number_guard.ts check E2 hard-fails on a duplicate LEADING NUMBER across both directories, precisely because the number 'is not a key of anything — it is a human coordination token, and nothing enforced it' (guard header, documenting the 467 precedent). So: SAFE FOR THE RUNNER, NOT SAFE FOR CI. The failure is deferred, not absent — it fires when both branches reach main, and on whichever PR merges second, which is not the PR that owns the bug. My D-5 'do not renumber' conclusion survives; my reason for calling it safe was too narrow, and a binding ruling that says 'safe' on a partial mechanism sweep is exactly the defect this campaign exists to remove. (2) RENUMBERING IS REFUSED, BOTH WAYS, and this is a refusal rather than a park. Renumbering OUR file: it is applied to production; renaming an applied migration breaks the filename key the ledger and drift-detector depend on, and engages H5. Renumbering P4-I'S file: same H5 objection, PLUS it is another campaign's artifact outside this mandate — that is P2 scope-widening and would not be mine even if H5 did not bite. SUTRADHARA was right that at minimum the p4-i option is not ours, and right to decline to choose. (3) THE DISCLOSED-ADDITIONS ROUTE IS GRANTED, and it is expressly NOT an H3 weakening of a CI guard. I checked the mechanism before granting rather than accepting the recommendation: migration_number_legacy_duplicates.json's own _README states that legacy_duplicate_groups is frozen and immutable, and that 'a collision that lands AFTER the freeze, owned by a campaign this guard's own lane does not control, is NOT added here — it goes in disclosed_additions instead: one itemized, dated, attributed entry per number (Dvarapala RULING 70), same discipline as schema_validator.py's known_residuals.' subject: The poke mechanism manufactures the stalls it detects — stall-state taxonomy corrected
question: SUTRADHARA root-caused the PARIKSAKA 'stall': the agent was IDLE, not stuck. tmux send-keys without a separate submit writes the poke into the compose box and stops there, so the agent never sees it, stays silent, and PRAHARI reads the continued silence as a worsening stall. Does this change the stall rule?
ruling: YES, AND THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT FLEET FINDING SO FAR. THE DETECTOR WAS MANUFACTURING THE CONDITION IT DETECTED — a closed loop that would have produced 'stalls' indefinitely, escalating forever on evidence it created itself. That is not a monitoring bug; it is the campaign's own founding defect wearing fleet clothing, and it is the exact class §N.8 names: an action taken on a signal with nothing real behind it. It is also, as SUTRADHARA notes, the same defect as the launcher's original unsubmitted kick prompt — fixed in nirmana-up.sh, never fixed in the poke path. THREE BINDING RULINGS. (1) A NEW STATE EXISTS AND MUST BE DISTINGUISHED: IDLE-UNPOKED. A pane showing a COMPLETED turn with text sitting at the compose prompt is IDLE-UNPOKED, not stalled. Its remedy is to SUBMIT THE BOX — one keystroke. It is NEVER a restart. A restart here would have destroyed a live, healthy PARIKSAKA holding 13 queued reports and two filed verdicts, to fix a problem that needed an Enter. Byte-identical successive captures are evidence of this state, not of a hang: nothing was computing and nothing was going to. (2) A POKE MUST BE VERIFIED DELIVERED, and the mechanics are not the obvious ones. SUTRADHARA measured that a bare 'send-keys C-m' against a box already holding text DID NOT WORK — recorded here because the obvious fix fails and would otherwise be adopted and trusted. The sequence that works: send-keys C-u (clear any stranded fragment, which would otherwise be prepended to the next poke), sleep 1, send-keys '<text>', sleep 2, then send-keys Enter as a SEPARATE call after a settle. AFTER POKING, CAPTURE THE PANE AGAIN AND CONFIRM THE TEXT IS GONE FROM THE PROMPT. An unverified poke is an action with no detector behind it, which is precisely what this campaign exists to refuse — and PRAHARI must never escalate on silence that followed a poke it did not confirm landed. (3) PRAHARI'S CONDUCT WAS CORRECT AND IS COMMENDED ON THE RECORD. It escalated instead of restarting, which is what D-1(c) required, and that judgement is the only reason a healthy PARIKSAKA still exists with its context intact. Its escalation was right on the evidence available; the evidence was an artifact of the tooling, which is not a monitoring failure. This ruling does NOT relax D-1(c): PRAHARI still does not restart on silence. It now has a third option between 'ignore' and 'escalate' — submit the box and verify — and one more reason to distrust silence as a signal. D-1(c)'s suspension of restart-on-silence remains in force until the heartbeat defect is fixed AND a heartbeat has been observed from every agent.

subject: F-SEEDER-DEAD — which surface owns registry metadata; bg_cohort is a safety interlock
question: PARIKSAKA V-5: asset_registry_seed.ts exits 1 on every invocation (bg_cohort's COHORT_SIZE formula), and asks which surface owns the registry metadata that §8.6 stage 2 Conform must write for every asset in every rung — the seeder or migrations — since either answer implies a problem (Conform blocked, or silent divergence).

I read the seeder's upsert rather than reason about it, and the decisive fact is in neither escalation: asset_registry_seed.ts:3215-3245's ON CONFLICT (asset_id) DO UPDATE SET INCLUDES target_floor, depends_on, count_sql, volume_explanation AND scope. Every one of those is a field §8.6 stage 2 Conform is REQUIRED to write, per rung, from measurement. SO THE HAZARD IS NOT DIVERGENCE, IT IS SILENT REVERSION: any seeder run after a rung's Conform stage overwrites that rung's measured floors, its DAG edges, its cockpit count_sql and its by-design volume_explanations with whatever the TS file happens to declare — no error, no warning, exit 0. That would destroy completed campaign work in a way nothing currently detects. (1) THE OWNERSHIP RULING, and I am reading it out of the plan rather than inventing it, because I7 has already decided it: a target_floor is set to the MEASURED ACHIEVED COUNT. A declarative source file structurally CANNOT hold a measured value — it can only hold a value someone typed, which is precisely the stale-historical-figure failure I7 exists to forbid. Therefore the line is: DECLARED values belong to the seeder (asset_id, layer, sort_order, names, descriptions, storage_type, target_table, asset_type); MEASURED and CAMPAIGN-ADJUDICATED values belong to the campaign and MUST NOT appear in the seeder's SET clause (target_floor, integrity_check_sql, domain, rung, partition declarations, consumers, and volume_explanation where it records a G4 by-design classification). Schema — the columns themselves — remains migrations'. This is not a new architecture; it is the only reading under which I7 and the seeder can both be true. (2) REQUIRED CHANGE, AND THE CODEBASE ALREADY CONTAINS ITS PATTERN. target_floor must be removed from the DO UPDATE SET clause or guarded so a re-seed cannot lower or overwrite a campaign-set value. THE PRECEDENT IS IN THE SAME SET CLAUSE, EIGHT LINES BELOW: the MR-06 RETIRED guard, which reads 'A RETIRED asset must NEVER be resurrected by a re-seed... preserve that status rather than blindly overwriting with whatever the seed says.' The shape is identical — a re-seed must never revert a measured floor — so the fix is to extend an existing, reviewed, in-file discipline rather than invent one. Same treatment for domain/rung/integrity_check_sql BEFORE they are ever added to the seeder; note they are currently safe only because 590 has not applied and the seeder does not yet know those columns exist. (3) THE SYNTHESIS THAT MATTERS MOST — bg_cohort IS A LOAD-BEARING SAFETY INTERLOCK, NOT A ONE-LINE BUG. Three separate silent-damage paths are TODAY held back by nothing but that formula error: (a) the import hazard M0-T15 closed, which would have reached INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE on asset_registry; (b) D-17's phantom DRY_RUN, where the documented command pairs the flag with $PROD_DB_URL and the flag does not exist; (c) this one, silent reversion of every Conform field. ALL THREE ARE UNLOCKED BY THE SAME ONE-LINE FIX. This is the third instance today of the shape I first recorded in D-9 — luck standing in for a guard — and it is now a pattern rather than a coincidence: this codebase repeatedly holds a hazard shut with something that was never meant to be a lock. RULING: bg_cohort's formula bug MUST NOT BE REPAIRED until all three hazards are independently closed. It stays pinned to rungs.R0.stage2_carry_forward as SUTRADHARA correctly placed it (I13 forbids touching it anyway, R0 being unopened), but its pin must now carry this warning, because the danger is that someone — an R0 KARAKA, or an unrelated session finding a broken seeder — repairs the obvious thing and silently arms three loaded mechanisms in one commit. It must land BEFORE R0's Conform stage opens, which is what PARIKSAKA correctly identified as the real deadline. The per-field finalisation of the declared/measured split for the remaining columns is R0 stage-2 work and starts from this ruling rather than from scratch. (5) T15 CERTIFICATION ACCEPTED (V-5 PASS, 7 angles): own bidirectional mutation with byte-copy restore and sha256 identity, both pre-existing importers located independently and re-run 15/15, and the observable correctly identified as strictly stronger than its sibling's because validateFormulas() logs before any pg.Client exists. subject: F-3 — migrate.ts --target is a stop-after bound, not a select-one filter; D-9 part 2 corrected
question: KARAKA-M0-T12 halted the migration wave before applying anything: --target does not SELECT a migration, it only bounds where the run STOPS, so the dispatched sequence 589->588->590 with each --target pinned is mechanically impossible. Which option proceeds?

(1) I CORRECT D-9 PART 2, AND THE CORRECTION IS THE IMPORTANT PART OF THIS RULING. I wrote that 590 must be applied with --target pinned 'so the run cannot sweep anything else.' THE CONDITION WAS RIGHT AND MY STATED REASON WAS FALSE. --target bounds only the TAIL of the run, never the HEAD (migrate.ts:625-681 iterates every collected file in global sorted order and applies each unapplied one, checking 'file.name === target' only AFTER the apply, to break; there is no filter on target anywhere in runMigrations, and collectMigrationFiles:400-411 merges both directories sorted globally by localeCompare). Since 590 is the HIGHEST-sorting unapplied file, '--target 590' excludes nothing whatsoever — it would have applied 588, 589 and 590. The KARAKA proved it live rather than by reading: a --dry-run pinned to 589 printed all three. So my ruling contained an ASSERTED PROPERTY WITH NO DETECTOR BEHIND IT — §N.8, arising inside a binding ruling rather than inside code. That is the fourth instance of this shape today and the first that is mine. I record it in exactly those terms because a ledger that catches the code's unearned claims while protecting its own is worth nothing, and because the fleet must stay willing to do to my rulings what this KARAKA just did. (2) WHY OPTION A IS CORRECT AND NOT MERELY AVAILABLE. --target DOES deliver D-9's intent, but only under the condition the KARAKA identified: files applied in ascending order, one run per file. Then each run's target is also the LOWEST unapplied file, so the loop applies exactly one migration and breaks — one migration, one ledger row, and the orders' after-check ('exactly one new _migrations_applied row') becomes meaningful instead of failing by construction. (3) THE COST OF RELEASING 589-FIRST IS EMPIRICALLY NEAR ZERO, WHICH IS WHY I RELEASE IT RATHER THAN RE-ENGINEER AROUND IT. The dispatch put 589 first so the flag would be rehearsed on a pure DROP ... IF EXISTS before touching 588's unscoped DELETE FROM build_protected_assets. Sound reasoning in the abstract, but I verified in D-5 that 588 is ALREADY A COMPLETE NO-OP IN CURRENT PRODUCTION STATE: 0 protection triggers, 0 of the 6 guard functions, and build_protected_assets empty — so its DROPs hit nothing and its DELETE targets an empty table. (4) THE PRECONDITION MOVES, AND THIS IS BINDING: D-10 part 4's check — build_protected_assets count(*) = 0 — is verified IMMEDIATELY BEFORE RUN 1 (588), not before a later step. The KARAKA's sharpest observation is that the dispatched sequence would have run 588's DELETE before the step where its own mandatory precondition sat: 'a precondition that is checked after the fact is not a precondition.' Exactly right, and that alone would have justified the halt even if --target had worked as I described. With Option A, 588 is first and its guard is checked immediately before it — the safety property is preserved, not traded away. (5) OPTIONS B AND C REFUSED. B (accept a two-migration first run) runs 588 before its precondition and destroys the one-row-per-run property that makes the after-check a detector at all. C (preserve 589-first literally) requires either changing migrate.ts — machinery not authorized for this task, and not wanted mid-wave — or registering 588 by direct ledger INSERT, which is precisely the method D-10 part 4 deliberately replaced with a real execution. (6) TWO THINGS RECORDED AS PRECEDENT, both from the KARAKA's honesty rather than my ruling. Second: V-3 does NOT certify selection semantics and PARIKSAKA never claimed it did — its angle 5 exercised --target against an unreachable database and observed only that main() was entered, which is a correct proof about the ENTRYPOINT GUARD and silent about selection. Nobody should later read V-3 as evidence about what --target selects. (7) PROCEED. Every precondition holds and the D-4 condition 3 pre-flight detector PASSES 4/4 — the wave was blocked on the mechanism, not the data. Dispatch Option A.

ruling: D-21 IS REVERSED. THE CHALLENGE IS CORRECT AND MY RULING WAS WRONG. I verified the decisive clause rather than take it on report: NIRMANA_ELEVATION_PLAN_v4_0.md:862, the §8.4 R5 row, reads '...zero-row-by-design assets recorded honestly with target_floor = 0 and a volume_explanation rather than left reading dormant; LEL_EVENTS RECLASSIFIED SOURCE; the layer's two shared-domain members...'. The plan assigns this reclassification to R5, by name. WHY I WAS WRONG, AND IT IS MY OWN PRECEDENT THAT CONVICTS ME. D-21 rested on the claim that Phase 0.5b is an M0 deliverable, which it is under §14.4's general mapping ('Phase 0 — all 15 steps -> M0'). But §8.4's R5 row is a SPECIFIC assignment of this exact reclassification to a specific rung, and in D-12 I ruled — on the ka_gochara_sweep zombie rows, against an M0 exit criterion that appeared to demand them — that 'a specific assignment governs a general exit criterion'. That reasoning applies here identically and I failed to apply it to myself eleven rulings later. Applying my own precedent to SUTRADHARA's question and not to this one is exactly the inconsistency the charter warns is most of what delegated authority actually is. THE SECOND ERROR, WHICH IS WORSE BECAUSE IT IS DOCTRINAL: D-21 carefully separated 'making SOURCE expressible' from 'reclassifying any asset', and granted the first. But if the only SOURCE reclassification the plan schedules is lel_events, and that is R5, then NOTHING IN M0 NEEDS THE CHECK WIDENED — and widening it now is building infrastructure for a later phase, which CLAUDE.md forbids outright ('Pre-build infrastructure for macro-phases later than the currently-active one', MACRO_PLAN §Scope Boundary). My 'expressible vs exercised' distinction was a real distinction that did no work: it licensed the pre-build rather than preventing it. RULING: the CHECK widening for SOURCE is R5 CONFORM work and is not authorized now. Phase 0.5b does NOT close in M0; it is recorded as deferred-to-R5 with this reason, honestly and not as a green (G7). G1's SOURCE disposition therefore remains unexercisable until R5, which is not a defect in the charter but the ladder working — the power exists for when its rung opens. M0's own SOURCE-BLOCKED thread closes on this ruling rather than on a repair. I ALSO AFFIRM WHAT M0-T8 DID WHILE BLOCKED, which is the part that deserves the most credit: it held lel_events's layer_index and layer_name NULL rather than guess, because the correct value is NULL-if-source but L5/Mimamsa-if-data and is therefore not mechanically derivable — so D-4 condition 2 and H6 both bite. That is M0-T2's data_disposition precedent applied without being told to, which is what precedent working looks like from below. TO THE FLEET: in D-20 I wrote that the fleet must stay willing to do to my rulings what a KARAKA had just done. One did so within the hour, on a ruling of mine less than an hour old, and was right. That invitation was not rhetorical and this reversal is the proof.

subject: has_substeps repair (Phase 0.6a) — SATYA-DIPA's defect still live on 12 assets; and the 0.6b ordering trap
question: M0-T8 verified asset_runner.py:620 reads has_substeps from asset_registry and initialises plan_complete=True, recomputing it only inside 'if has_substeps:'. So 12 assets (8 CURRENT) whose writers genuinely plan substeps have the completeness re-probe switched OFF and are promoted lit on a partial build. SUTRADHARA wants explicit authorization because it is the one M0 write that changes build-promotion behaviour. Separately: the plan's 0.6b wording, applied literally, would corrupt two rows.
ruling: TWO PARTS, BOTH GRANTED. (1) THE has_substeps REPAIR IS AUTHORIZED, AND IT IS NOT OPTIONAL. Phase 0.6a names it M0 content; it is a write to asset_registry, which is registry metadata and squarely inside I14; and no rung is open to be trespassed. But the decisive point is not scope, it is that THE CURRENT STATE IS A LIVE H4 VIOLATION. asset_runner.py:620 initialises plan_complete=True and only recomputes it inside 'if has_substeps:', so for these 12 rows the substep-plan-completeness detector NEVER RUNS and lit is written on a basis that is not its detector's verdict. That is H4 verbatim, and it is CLAUDE.md §N.8's fourth named instance — the one SATYA-DIPA fixed in code on 2026-07-29. The code fix landed; the registry rows that switch the question off were never repaired, SO THE FIX IS INERT ON EXACTLY THE ASSETS IT WAS BUILT FOR. A detector that exists and is being told not to run is not a detector. Leaving it is the violation; repairing it is the campaign doing its job. SUTRADHARA'S CAUTION IS ANSWERED DIRECTLY, and this is binding: after the repair, twelve assets CAN fail to reach lit that currently always do. THAT IS THE CORRECT OUTCOME AND IT IS NOT A REGRESSION. An asset that stops reaching lit was never entitled to lit — it was being promoted past a check nobody was running. NO AGENT MAY 'FIX' A RESULTING incomplete BY REVERTING has_substeps, and any such proposal is refused as H3 (disabling a gate to make something pass), not debated. If eight CURRENT assets go incomplete, that is eight true statements replacing eight false ones, and the honest cockpit reading is the deliverable. CONDITIONS: (a) THE MEASUREMENT GOVERNS, NOT THE PLAN'S FIGURE — 12 measured against the plan's 14, with both extras explained (bg_reference is a 51-line LIGHT writer with no plan_substeps at all; bo_laksana_rerank shares a file with the heavy BoLaksanaWriter). Repair the 12 that were measured; do not repair two more to reach a number, which would be H6. This is I7's discipline applied to a count instead of a floor. (b) THE DISCRIMINATING DETECTOR MUST PASS — bo_laksana true AND bo_laksana_rerank false. That pair catches file-granularity scoping, which is the exact error that produced the plan's phantom extras, so a proposal that cannot tell those two apart has not earned the repair. (c) 0 false positives were measured; confirm that no asset LOSES a legitimate has_substeps=true. (d) The write touches the has_substeps column ONLY, and NO BUILD IS DISPATCHED as part of this task — the changed promotion behaviour is observed at the next legitimate build, not provoked now. (e) PARIKSAKA verifies independently (I16), and verifies the DETECTOR now runs, not merely that the column changed. (2) THE 0.6b ORDERING TRAP: REPAIR VALUES FIRST, THEN MAKE THE COLUMN AUTHORITATIVE. M0-T8 is right and the plan's wording is a trap. All six asset_kind/asset_type disagreements resolve to 'service', but by two different routes — 2 need asset_kind corrected, 4 need asset_type corrected. Making asset_kind authoritative FIRST, applied literally as a repair rule, would write 'data' over a CORRECT 'service' on bg_ephemeris_engine and bg_panchanga. The plan's sentence is a statement about the END STATE, not an instruction for the ORDER of operations, and the two must not be conflated. Authorized order: repair the six values to their correct settings, THEN make the column authoritative. Recorded because it is instructive: this is a runtime no-op today (both live consumers read the pair as an OR), which is precisely why nothing has broken and why nothing would have noticed the corruption — the fourth instance today of a hazard sitting harmless behind an accident. (3) THE CI BLOCKING SWITCH IS NOT FLIPPED YET. SUTRADHARA correctly dispatched T9's guards NON-blocking and left the switch to me. It stays unflipped: several M0 exit criteria are legitimately non-zero right now, and flipping blocking while they are would halt all work — and the temptation that follows would be to weaken a criterion to get moving, which is H3. THE SWITCH FLIPS WHEN T17's EXIT SCORECARD SHOWS EACH CRITERION EITHER AT ZERO OR EXPLICITLY DEFERRED WITH A RECORDED REASON — never on a criterion that is merely unexamined. I also affirm T9's three instructions as binding standards for every guard this campaign ships: each guard carries a fixture proving it CAN fail, 'not_checkable' is a distinct outcome from 'pass', and no guard is wired blocking without my word. The first is §N.8 in its purest form and I want it on every guard, not just these.

subject: F-HASWRITER — a registry boolean lying to the efficiency gate; V-6 closes V-1; V-7 confirms D-20
question: PARIKSAKA V-6: two R0 assets (bg_nakshatra_medical, bg_transit_engine) carry has_writer=false while the code carries @register for both, so _bound_class() reads 'not-a-build' and EXEMPTS them from the §8.3 item 5 efficiency pass entirely. Confirmed 2 false negatives, 0 false positives. Needs a Defect Register entry and a fix.
ruling: CONFIRMED AND GRANTED, SPLIT BY RUNG — and the generalisation matters more than the two cells. (1) THE DEFECT IS REAL AND IT IS A GATE BYPASS AT THE FIRST FREEZE. §8.3 item 5 lets an asset freeze either optimized-with-identity-proof or 'examined, already efficient', but 'not-a-build' exempts it from the efficiency pass ALTOGETHER. Two genuinely-built R0 assets would therefore walk through the campaign's very first freeze gate unexamined — the precise unearned-signal defect the §19 ledger was written to remove, hiding in the one §19 field that is not uniformly null. PARIKSAKA is right that this is NOT the builder's fault: _bound_class()'s logic ('no registered writer -> nothing builds this asset') is sound; its INPUT is wrong, because build_asset_control_workbook.py:91 reads has_writer straight from asset_registry instead of deriving it from the writer class. The builder described the registry accurately and the registry lied to it. (2) THE FIX IS THE GENERATOR, AND IT IS SUFFICIENT — SPLIT: (a) IN M0, NOW: change the workbook generator to DERIVE has_writer from the writer class, exactly as it already code-scans has_substeps, and carry both a '(registry)' and a '(code)' column for it as the workbook already does for substeps. This is generator machinery, data-neutral, writes nothing to asset_registry, and is squarely M0. It is also NECESSARY AND SUFFICIENT to close the gate bypass: with a code-derived flag the two assets read bound class = null rather than not-a-build, so they are no longer exempted and R0's freeze will demand their efficiency pass. (b) PINNED TO R0, NOT DONE NOW: correcting the two asset_registry.has_writer ROWS. Those are L0 assets and has_writer is NOT among the derived fields M0's Phase 0.6a names (layer position, kind, has_substeps) — so unlike D-24 I have no named M0 mandate to write them, and reaching into R0's registry metadata on my own reading is the exact error I just reversed myself for in D-23. The generator fix closes the hazard; the row repair belongs to R0 stage 2 (Conform), which owns R0's registry metadata, and it opens there with this measurement already in hand. (c) DO NOT SPECIAL-CASE THE TWO ASSET IDS. PARIKSAKA is right: hardcoding bg_nakshatra_medical and bg_transit_engine would fix the symptom and leave the mechanism, and would silently miss the next secondary decorator on a shared writer class. Both these cases ARE secondary decorators on a shared class, which is the general shape. (3) THE GENERALISATION, WHICH IS THE REAL FINDING. This is the SAME DEFECT CLASS AS D-24, one column over: a REGISTRY BOOLEAN THAT DISAGREES WITH THE CODE AND, WHEN FALSE, SILENTLY DISABLES A CHECK. has_substeps=false switches off the substep-plan-completeness probe (D-24, §N.8 instance 4); has_writer=false switches off the efficiency pass (this). The workbook ALREADY carries dual registry/code columns for has_substeps precisely because that divergence is a known defect — it is D-01 — and the identical defect for has_writer has never been named. STANDING RULE, binding beyond these two columns: ANY REGISTRY BOOLEAN THAT GATES WHETHER A CHECK RUNS MUST BE DERIVED FROM CODE, NEVER TRUSTED AS DECLARED, and must be surfaced as a registry-vs-code PAIR so the divergence is visible rather than silently authoritative. A declared flag that can turn a detector off is itself an unearned signal, and the plan's own M0 sweep should look for others of this shape rather than wait to trip over them. Defect Register entry authorized as D-01's sibling, via the GENERATOR's input (§16: generated, never hand-edited). (4) V-1 IS CLOSED. V-6 PASS accepted: 11 sheets, all nine §16 columns, the five absent fields at 128/128, 'no bespoke speed work' 64->0, hotspot null on 128/128, and timeout-source 107 registered / 21 default matching the live distribution PARIKSAKA measured itself in V-2. D-8's per-template precision HELD IN BOTH DIRECTIONS and was measured rather than eyeballed: the 8 'not-a-build' and 40 'built once' carve-outs survived intact, and of the 64 swept assets ZERO lost a measured line, a ledger line or a p50, with no block shorter than its pre-T5 version. I asked for a hunt in both directions and got one. I also accept the withdrawn rows/sec challenge: PARIKSAKA checked the premise rather than deferring and found build_run_assets genuinely has no row-count column, so null is the doctrine correctly applied. (5) V-7 ACCEPTED — it independently confirms D-20 against live production (447 ledger rows unchanged; no row for 588/589/590; of 590's target columns only integrity_check_sql pre-exists, so nothing partially applied) and notes the trap that the 588_samiksha row is the OTHER 588 and is not evidence of an apply. D-20 stands unaltered; the wave proceeds under Option A. (6) TWO SELF-CORRECTIONS I WANT ON THE RECORD, both PARIKSAKA's: its first reading blamed a fuzzy filename match in the Writer File column and it CHECKED BEFORE REPORTING, finding the column right and the bound class wrong — the opposite of its hypothesis; and it flagged its own confused sentence about the disjoint 8/5 sets while affirming the data. Corrections made before reporting rather than after are the standard this campaign runs on, and this is the third time today an agent has met it.

subject: G-03 — deriveState.ts returns service_ok ahead of every check, overriding a detector that fired
question: SUTRADHARA/M0-T24: deriveState.ts:65 returns 'service_ok' as the FIRST statement for any service asset, and plan.ts:196 READY_STATES makes that green dependency-satisfying. ka_graha_sancara ran its own self-test on 2026-08-02, wrote service_health='unhealthy', and still renders green. Is repairing generic serving code Track M, or does it wait for a rung?
ruling: CONFIRMED BY MY OWN INSPECTION AND GRANTED AS TRACK M, SPLIT INTO WHAT IS FORCED NOW AND WHAT IS M3's. I read the code rather than accept the report: deriveState.ts:65 is 'if (asset.asset_type === service || asset.asset_kind === service) return service_ok' and it IS the first statement — ahead of is_active, ahead of incomplete, ahead of error, ahead of actualRows. It is worse than reported in one respect nobody named: because it precedes the is_active check, an INACTIVE service also renders service_ok. plan.ts:196 READY_STATES = {lit, service_ok} and :250 treats a dep in that set as satisfied, so a service whose own detector said 'unhealthy' satisfies downstream build prerequisites. The function's comment states the claim it cannot support — 'they are healthy when registered + CURRENT' — while checking neither CURRENT nor anything else; four of the eight affected assets are not CURRENT. This is H4 in its purest form: not a green with no detector, but A GREEN OVERRIDING A DETECTOR THAT ALREADY RAN AND RETURNED THE OPPOSITE ANSWER. That is worse than every instance this campaign has catalogued so far, because in the others no one had looked; here someone looked, wrote down 'unhealthy', and the serving layer discarded it. (1) SCOPE: THIS IS TRACK M AND DOES NOT WAIT FOR A RUNG — and SUTRADHARA's reasoning for distinguishing it from the ka_kshetra string (PARK-5) is correct and I adopt it as the test. For PARK-5 the two scope tests CONFLICT: §8.2's bright-line ('does it change rows in an asset's target table') says Track M, while Track M's definition ('layer-independent machinery') says no, because that string is about one asset and repairing it well needs R3's understanding. That conflict is why PARK-5 is parked. HERE BOTH TESTS AGREE: deriveState is generic code governing every service asset in every layer (R0's two, R3's three, R5's two), no single rung owns it, it changes no asset's rows, and repairing it needs no asset-specific knowledge whatsoever — it needs the function to consult the detector instead of a declared string. Where both tests agree there is no invariant exception to make, so no P7 arises and PARK-5's parking is not weakened by this grant. If it waited for a rung it would wait for R5, and until then a service_ok outranking an 'unhealthy' reading keeps satisfying dependencies. (2) FORCED NOW, AND NOT OPTIONAL: deriveState MUST NOT RETURN service_ok WHEN A REAL DETECTOR VERDICT EXISTS AND SAYS OTHERWISE. ka_graha_sancara's stored 'unhealthy' must win over the declared type/kind. This requires no design judgement and closes the H4. The early return must also stop preceding the is_active check. (3) DEFERRED TO M3, DELIBERATELY: what a service with NO probe should render, and whether that state belongs in READY_STATES. Five of the eight have a NULL health_probe, so there is no verdict to consult, and the honest answer is 'unknown' rather than either green or red — but choosing that vocabulary and deciding whether unknown satisfies a dependency is exactly the integrity-gate engine's territory, which §14.1 assigns to M3 ('writes lit only on pass'). I will not pre-build it (the D-23 lesson). Recording the shape now so M3 inherits it rather than rediscovers it. (4) MANDATORY PRE-FLIGHT, in the D-4 condition-3 pattern that has now worked twice: BEFORE applying, MEASURE and report which assets change rendered state and which downstream dependencies would stop being satisfied. IF ANY CURRENTLY-DISPATCHABLE BUILD WOULD BE BLOCKED, RETURN TO ME BEFORE WRITING. An asset that stops satisfying a dependency was never entitled to satisfy it — that is D-24's logic and it holds — but the blast radius must be measured, not discovered. No rung is open and no build is running, which makes this the safest possible moment. (5) D-24 AND D-25 ARE EXTENDED — their repairs do not reach the consumers M0-T24 found, and a fix that covers one language and not the other is not a fix: has_substeps ALSO at classifyStuckCandidate.ts:71-73, where the TypeScript reaper promotes a stuck asset to 'lit' — the same defect as D-24 in a different language, and D-24's Python-side repair leaves it live; has_writer ALSO at runs/route.ts:139 and recalibrationEnqueue.ts:140, governing BUILD-PLAN MEMBERSHIP, not merely the efficiency pass D-25 addressed. Both are covered by their original rulings' conditions. (6) COMMENDED, and it is the part that makes this verdict usable: M0-T24 kept tier A (a flag contradicting the code) apart from tier B (a flag with no code to contradict) and said plainly that folding them together would have turned ONE new instance into SIX. Of 40 columns examined, 8 gate a detector, 2 were already ruled, 6 are new, and exactly ONE is the known shape. A sweep that reports one finding where six were available is doing the work honestly. Its self-correction is the third of this exact form today: its scanner reported 3 has_writer divergences against PARIKSAKA's 0 false positives, and it debugged ITS OWN SCANNER rather than the registry, finding mi_sankalpa.py:76's @register(ASSET_ID) module-constant form that its regex could not match. It discarded the phantom and wrote the trap into both deliverables. (7) TIER B RECORDED FOR M3, NOT ACTED ON: integrity_check_sql is NULL on 128/128 and rebuild_on_probe_fail is false on 128/128 — the integrity gate is switched off at two independent columns. Correctly classified as tier B (a declaration that can only be justified, never derived), so it is not the D-25 shape and needs no sweep; it is the CONDITION M3's gate engine will be built to read, and M3 should expect to find the gate off everywhere rather than assume a baseline. (8) ONE THING I NOTICED THAT NOBODY RAISED, flagged as a question and not ruled: plan.ts:250 reads 'if (depState === undefined || READY_STATES.has(depState)) continue' — an UNDEFINED dependency state also satisfies the check. That may well be deliberate for cross-layer scoping, and I have not verified the intent, so I am not ruling on it. PARIKSAKA should examine whether 'unknown means ready' is intended there or is the same defect shape one line over.

subject: Seed-vs-DB ownership of registry metadata — measured; D-19 refined into three classes
question: M0-T29 completed the durability register: 23 of 23 seed-overwritten columns modelled, 0 UNKNOWN, a re-seed moves 260 cells across 96 assets. Three exposures remain and the register states it has NO BASIS to decide which side is right for 80 cells of count_sql / target_floor / depends_on. That is D-19's question with a number attached. How is it settled, and at every rung?
ruling: D-19'S PRINCIPLE STANDS AND IS NOW REFINED INTO THREE CLASSES, BECAUSE THE MEASUREMENT SHOWS TWO WERE NOT ENOUGH. First the reassuring half, which the register reported plainly rather than manufacturing risk to justify itself: MOST CAMPAIGN REPAIRS ARE DURABLE. domain, rung, superseded_by, data_disposition, has_substeps, has_writer, integrity_check_sql, clear_tables, service_health and writer_timeout_seconds appear in NEITHER of the seed's column lists. So D-19's alarm was correctly raised and is correctly narrowed by evidence — which is what measurement is for. (1) THE THIRD CLASS D-19 MISSED. I split registry fields into DECLARED (seed owns) and MEASURED (campaign owns, must leave the SET clause). The 80 cells prove a third exists, and it is why the register honestly reported no basis to choose: DECLARED-BUT-VERIFIABLE — a value that is legitimately authored in source AND checkable against reality. count_sql and depends_on are exactly this. A DAG edge SHOULD be declared in source, where it is reviewable and diffable, and SHOULD be audited against what the code actually reads (that is SQ-01's whole purpose); it should not live only in a database where no diff shows it changing. So neither surface is unconditionally right, and the register was correct to refuse to pick — the error would have been picking. (2) THE RULING, PER CLASS. (a) MEASURED — target_floor. Campaign owns it; it must leave the seed's DO UPDATE SET or be guarded MR-06-style. I7 sets a floor to the MEASURED ACHIEVED COUNT and a declarative file structurally cannot hold a measured value, so seed ownership of this column collides with I7 at EVERY rung, exactly as SUTRADHARA framed it. D-19 stands, now with a number behind it. (b) DECLARED-BUT-VERIFIABLE — count_sql, depends_on. They STAY in the seed as the declaration. What must change is that DIVERGENCE IS NEVER SILENTLY RESOLVED BY WHOEVER RUNS LAST: a seed run must produce a divergence report for these columns before writing, and the divergence is reconciled at the owning rung's Conform, on the merits, per cell. This is D-25's rule applied one layer over — declare in source, verify independently, SURFACE THE PAIR rather than let one side quietly win. (c) OPERATIONAL COROLLARY, FORCED BY THE EVIDENCE AND EASY TO MISS: a Conform repair to a declared-but-verifiable field MUST LAND IN BOTH SURFACES, or in the seed alone. Writing depends_on to the DB while the seed still declares the old value simply recreates the reversion this register was built to find. Every rung's Conform stage inherits this; it is not an M0 special case. (3) THE TWO OTHER EXPOSURES, BOTH FIXED IN M0. (a) asset_kind/asset_type: EIGHT rows, not six, because NOT ONE of the eight seed entries declares the key at all and assetKind/assetType DEFAULT TO 'data' when omitted (:3268). THE DEFAULT IS AN ACTIVE WRITE, NOT A NO-OP — modelling an absent column as 'unchanged' would have reported 0 and produced a falsely reassuring register. That trap is the single most valuable thing in this deliverable and I want it stated in the ledger, because 'absent means unchanged' is the intuition everyone brings and it is wrong here. Fix: declare BOTH keys explicitly in all eight entries so the default can never fire. (b) mi_jivanaghatana: live scope=per_chart/domain=chart, seed declares scope:'global'; scope is seed-overwritten and domain is not, so a re-seed moves ONE HALF OF A DERIVED PAIR and leaves the row internally inconsistent. This is a new sub-shape worth naming — not reversion but DESYNCHRONISATION OF A DERIVED PAIR — and any column pair where one half is seed-owned and the other campaign-owned has it latent. Fix the seed's declaration to match the measured truth; and check for other split pairs. (4) NOT WALL-CLOCK URGENT, AND I AM SAYING SO EXPLICITLY SO NOBODY RUSHES IT: the seeder still cannot complete a run because of the bg_cohort abort, so nothing can revert anything today. That is the same interlock D-19 identified holding a third hazard, and it reinforces rather than weakens D-19's ruling that bg_cohort must not be repaired until all of them are closed. The seed-ownership fixes must land BEFORE R0's Conform opens, which remains the real deadline. (5) SUTRADHARA'S SELF-CORRECTION ON 0.5a IS AFFIRMED AND IS THE RIGHT INSTINCT. It held 0.5a believing layer_index/layer_name would be reverted; the register showed the SEED HOLDS THE CLEAN VALUE on all 41 divergent cells, so the risk ran the OPPOSITE way — a re-seed would REPAIR those columns — and a DB repair to the clean value is therefore durable. subject: Deliberate-NULL category; restore drill standardised; DRY_RUN argv half; bg_sky_calendar self-deactivation; extracted-literal method
question: Five items from SUTRADHARA: (a) a re-seed would fill lel_events's deliberately-NULL layer_index/layer_name with L5/Mimamsa, silently answering a question D-23 reserved to R5; (b) M0-T26 EXECUTED a restore drill (transaction, compare, rollback) — did it exceed its instruction, and should the drill be standard?; (c) the argv half of the DRY_RUN hazard; (d) a re-seed would deactivate bg_sky_calendar; (e) does evaluating an inertness-proven extracted ASSETS literal violate D-13's import prohibition?
ruling: SIX PARTS. (1) A NEW CATEGORY, AND SUTRADHARA IS RIGHT THAT IT IS NOT THE DURABILITY PROBLEM: A DELIBERATE NULL ENCODING AN UNDECIDED QUESTION. M0-T2 and M0-T8 held lel_events's layer_index/layer_name at NULL because the correct value is NULL-if-source but L5/Mimamsa-if-data, and D-23 reserved that to R5 — so the NULL is not absent data, it is THE ONLY PLACE IN THE REGISTRY WHERE THE OPENNESS OF A RESERVED DECISION IS WRITTEN DOWN. A re-seed fills it with one of the two candidate answers, invisibly, and the resulting row is indistinguishable from a correctly-derived one. No value-drift measurement could flag it, because nothing was wrong before or after — which is exactly why it needs naming rather than measuring. THE FIX IS GENERAL AND FOLDS INTO D-27, NOT A SPECIAL CASE FOR lel_events (D-25 refused special-casing and I hold to that): D-27's mandatory seed divergence report MUST TREAT A NULL->VALUE TRANSITION AS A DISTINCT CATEGORY FROM A VALUE->VALUE CHANGE. Filling a NULL is not the same operation as changing a value; it is precisely where an undecided question gets silently answered by a default. Any NULL->value transition in that report requires an explicit decision before the seed runs, not after. (2) THE RESTORE DRILL: AUTHORIZED, AND MADE A STANDING REQUIREMENT FOR THIS CLASS OF REPAIR. M0-T26 did not exceed its instruction. 'Write only layer_index and layer_name, only on the measured rows' governs the NET EFFECT on the database, and the net effect was exactly that — the drill ran inside a transaction, compared (0 of 128 rows differed from the snapshot), rolled back, and re-ran its post-checks afterwards, which still pass. Nothing was net-written. More to the point, IT IS THE THING I DEMANDED IN D-7: I ruled that 'verified restorable with pg_restore -l' is not verification because -l never reads a data block, and that a real rehearsal must pass. Every prior repair in this campaign left its restore authored-but-unexercised. This KARAKA converted I2 from a ritual into a detector, which is the whole point, and it disclosed the action unprompted while naming it as the one it expected to be challenged. STANDING REQUIREMENT for repairs of this class, with conditions: the drill runs inside an explicit transaction that is ALWAYS rolled back and never committed; post-checks re-run after the rollback; the execution is disclosed in the report. CARVE-OUT, and it is not negotiable: THIS DOES NOT REACH THE GOCHARA CORPUS OR ANY P1 ASSET. There the stakes differ in kind, P1 reserves the operation to the native, and D-7's rehearsal standard for that snapshot requires my specific G6 approval and a scratch database — not a rollback drill against production. SUTRADHARA was right to flag its own reading as self-serving since it set the constraint, and right to ask rather than resolve it. (3) THE ARGV HALF OF THE DRY_RUN HAZARD — D-17 IS EXTENDED, AND I MEASURED IT: asset_registry_seed.ts HAS NO ARGV PARSING WHATSOEVER. 'argv' appears in that file ONLY inside M0-T15's entrypoint guard. So 'npx tsx scripts/seed/asset_registry_seed.ts --dry-run' does not error on an unrecognised flag — IT IGNORES IT AND RUNS A FULL LIVE UPSERT, exactly as the DRY_RUN env var does. D-17's ordered refusal must therefore trip on BOTH CHANNELS: the DRY_RUN environment variable AND an argv --dry-run (and its obvious spellings). An operator reaching for the flag form is the same careful operator D-17 exists to protect, and a refusal that covers only the channel we happened to find first is half a guard. (4) bg_sky_calendar: CONFIRMED, NOW TRIGGER-BEARING, STILL UNTOUCHED. I verified :3228 — if to_regclass finds no target_table the seed sets is_active=false. bg_sky_calendar is live is_active=true with target_table 'bg_sky_events', a relation absent from production, so a routine re-seed SWITCHES THE ASSET OFF. This is the second consequence of the phantom target_table M0-T6 pinned to R0; the first was that every count and integrity check authored for it would inherit a pointer to nothing. It remains L0 -> R0 -> not open -> UNTOUCHED (I13), but it is recorded as a defect with a TRIGGER rather than a latent one, and R0's intake must treat it as such. Note it is the fourth hazard whose only restraint is the bg_cohort abort — reinforcing D-19's interlock ruling again. AND I ADOPT SUTRADHARA'S LINE AS DOCTRINE: 'a guard that has never had to choose is not yet a detector.' The MR-06 RETIRED guard has never been exercised — its only live RETIRED row is declared RETIRED in the seed too, so both branches agree and it has never had to choose. That is the §N.8 shape one level up: not a signal without a detector, but a DETECTOR WITHOUT A DECISION. It also matters concretely, because D-19 directed the target_floor fix to be modelled on that guard: modelling on an unexercised guard means the model must be PROVEN by fixture, not inherited. (5) THE EXTRACTED-LITERAL METHOD DOES NOT VIOLATE D-13, and the KARAKA was right to ask. D-13 prohibits IMPORTING from asset_registry_seed.ts because the import executes main() and writes to asset_registry. Slicing out the ASSETS literal, proving it inert by machine, and evaluating that alone executes no module, runs no main(), and opens no connection — the hazard the prohibition names is structurally absent. The prohibition is on the EXECUTION PATH, not on the file's bytes; D-13 itself says 'read it, or parse it, or copy what you need'. This is parsing, done more rigorously than asked, with the inertness PROVEN rather than assumed. That proof is the condition: an extracted literal must be machine-proved inert before evaluation, every time. (6) RECORDED, BOTH WORTH THE LEDGER. The codepoint pin caught a REAL §N.1 violation BEFORE the write: production held ASCII-folded 'Ganita' (6/6) and 'Kala' (4/4) where §N.1's LOCKED lexicon has 'Gaṇita' (6/8) and 'Kala' with a long a (4/5). A detector built to fail, that failed, on the locked external lexicon — and caught it pre-write rather than post. And asset_runner.py:67's COALESCE(asset_kind, asset_type) is already asset_kind-only since asset_kind is NOT NULL, so the proposal's 'runtime no-op' claim is TRUE BUT FOR THE WRONG REASON AND ONLY CIRCUMSTANTIALLY — the two bg_* rows' kind genuinely changed under deps_unsatisfied, a path unreachable only because both happen to have zero dependents. A no-op by accident rather than by design, for the third time today. The KARAKA declining step 5 with a real argument (nothing enforces C-14, its guard is non-blocking, asset_kind is NOT NULL DEFAULT 'data', and a service misrouted to _run_data_writer would be a live error not a no-op) and naming the two required edits while making neither is exactly right, and it independently reaches the same conclusion as D-24 part 2's ordering ruling.

subject: The named-field test stated as a rule; criterion 10's circularity and H2 collision; C-28 deferral; the disclosure prerequisite

I have already decided both halves without naming the principle: D-24 authorized the has_substeps repair BECAUSE Phase 0.6a names it; D-25 part 2(b) pinned the has_writer ROW repair to R0 BECAUSE 0.6a does not, and I said there that reaching into R0's registry metadata on my own reading was 'the exact error I just reversed myself for in D-23'. STATED IN FULL, with both refinements my later rulings added: A REGISTRY COLUMN IS M0's TO REPAIR IF AND ONLY IF (a) A PHASE-0 STEP OR M0's OWN ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA NAME IT — acceptance criteria count, per D-4, where 'every asset carrying domain and rung' named the change that creates those columns — AND (b) NO MORE-SPECIFIC PLAN CLAUSE ASSIGNS IT TO A LATER RUNG, in which case the specific governs the general, per D-12 (the gochara zombie rows) and D-23 (lel_events -> SOURCE at §8.4's R5 row). Absent (a), the column belongs to the rung that owns the asset, and repairing it in M0 is the I13 breach. I verified the rule against all five of my own registry rulings — has_substeps (M0), has_writer rows (R0), domain/rung (M0), layer_index/layer_name (M0), SOURCE CHECK (R5) — and it reproduces every one. Apply it to reclassify the 6 rules and 2 criteria. (2) CRITERION 10 SPLITS, AND ONLY HALF IS MINE. (a) THE CIRCULARITY IS MINE AND I FIX IT NOW: criterion 10 asks whether the guards are blocking, while D-24 part 3 conditions the flip on every criterion being at zero or deferred — so each waits on the other and the precondition is unsatisfiable. That knot is of my own making, so I untie it: CRITERION 10 IS EXCLUDED FROM ITS OWN PRECONDITION. A criterion may not gate itself; D-24 part 3 is read as 'every criterion OTHER THAN 10'. This is a self-reference carve-out, not a weakening — every other criterion still binds, and H3 still forbids relaxing any of them to get moving. (b) THE 'MERGED' HALF IS PARKED (PARK-6). 'Merged' means merged to main, and H2 prohibits any write to main absolutely, for every agent, unappealably. So M0's own exit criterion cannot be satisfied by this campaign at all. SUTRADHARA read this as a charter-versus-plan disagreement to be parked under the charter's own resolution clause, and that is right — with one thing made explicit, because 'the plan wins' could otherwise be read as licensing the merge: IT DOES NOT. H2 sits in §3, whose prohibitions are refused rather than parked and are not appealable, so no reading of 'the plan wins' authorizes a write to main, and I am not granting one. What is parked is how the criterion gets satisfied — by a merge performed outside this campaign, or by the native waiving it — not whether H2 bends. A deferral recorded only in DECISIONS.jsonl is invisible to the guard. AMENDED FLIP CONDITION: the switch flips when every criterion is at zero or deferred AND EVERY DEFERRED RULE CARRIES ITS DISCLOSURE ENTRY, itemized and dated, in the same discipline D-10 part 3 granted for the migration-number allowlist. The pressure that would otherwise follow a red branch is to weaken a criterion to get moving, which is H3 — so the disclosure work is what makes the flip possible without that pressure ever arising. Those are the 44- and 119-cell columns. A test whose first two candidate columns both fail it is not yet a test. subject: D-16's pane map corrected — address by session, never by pane; and restore a mutation from a byte-copy, never from git
question: (a) PRAHARI/SUTRADHARA report D-16's map entry 'SUTRADHARA=%0' is misleading: a keystroke to %0 lands in madhav-8e's compose box, not the conductor's, so an agent following D-16 literally would type into a session that is not the intended agent. That was right for the cross-wiring it addressed, and it is now insufficient for the same reason one layer over: %0 is a SECOND CASE WHERE THE ADDRESS DOES NOT IDENTIFY THE OCCUPANT. The first time a window NAME did not identify its content; this time a pane ID does not identify who receives the keystroke. An agent following D-16 literally, trying to reach SUTRADHARA, would type into madhav-8e. THE CORRECTED RULE: ADDRESS EVERY FLEET AGENT BY SESSION NAME VIA SendMessage, NEVER BY PANE. This removes the failure class rather than patching around it, which is what four idle-unpoked stalls argued for, and it is a shorter rule than the one it supersedes — a good sign. D-16's pane map is withdrawn as an addressing table; CAMPAIGN_STATE.fleet_addressing is now the record. WHAT SURVIVES D-16 UNCHANGED, and these are the parts that mattered: pane %15 IS NEVER TOUCHED, absolutely and for any reason, because it hosts another campaign's live session (P2); no agent kills, restarts or reorganises either tmux session; and killing prp-night still kills the conductor, which is PARK-4 and unaffected. PANE CAPTURE IS RETAINED AS THE CORROBORATING CHECK, NOT DISCARDED — PRAHARI's judgement here is right and worth stating: ListAgents' idle/busy is now the primary liveness signal, but THE PANE IS WHAT TELLS YOU WHY, and it was pane capture's 'completed turn with text at the prompt' observation that let D-14 name IDLE-UNPOKED at all. A cheaper primary signal does not retire the richer secondary one. (2) RESTORE A MUTATION FROM A BYTE-COPY, NEVER FROM GIT — STANDING INSTRUCTION, BINDING ON EVERY AGENT. FORBIDDEN for restoring a mutation: git checkout -- <file>, git restore <file>, git stash / stash pop, git checkout HEAD -- <path>. Each restores GIT's idea of the file rather than YOURS, and in a shared working tree that silently discards whatever a sibling has edited since the last commit. REQUIRED: cp the file to a .bytecopy BEFORE mutating; mutate; run the test; CONFIRM IT FAILS; cp the byte-copy back; PROVE THE RESTORE with cmp or sha256 QUOTED IN THE REPORT; delete the byte-copy. Step 4 is not optional — a restore you did not verify is the same unearned signal as a guard you never watched fail, and this campaign has now spent a day establishing that a claim without its check is worth nothing. THIS EXTENDS THE SHARED-TREE DISCIPLINE OF D-3/D-13/D-15 TO ITS THIRD SURFACE: those covered STAGING (path-scoped only) and COMMITTING (git commit --only, verified in D-15); this covers RESTORING. And it is the most dangerous of the three, because the other two leave an artifact — a wrong file in a commit, visible in the diff — whereas A LOST UNCOMMITTED EDIT LEAVES NOTHING TO NOTICE. The sibling finds out later, or never. I note it is already most agents' practice: PARIKSAKA's own V-3 and V-5 mutations were restored from byte-copies with sha256 quoted, which is why it recognised the hazard in the first place. Codifying an existing good practice before it is violated is cheaper than every alternative. (3) SUTRADHARA's NEW ESCALATION PRACTICE IS ALREADY WORKING AND I WANT THAT ON THE RECORD. This message marks exactly what it VERIFIED (ListAgents' own header; its process ancestry through %0's pane_pid 83558), what it DID NOT verify (which specific process is madhav-8e — it stopped rather than spend further because the operational answer did not depend on it), and what is a READING rather than a finding (that madhav-8e is the interactive session which launched it, explaining both the start-time gap and the shared ancestry — explicitly not proved). subject: target_floor leaves the INSERT list too; the I18 argument test adopted; wave recorded as defect-removal with null speedup; L-08 is M1's
question: V-12/V-13/V-14 raise four things for me: (a) target_floor remains in the seed's INSERT list — latent today, fires on the next new asset; (b) is a closed-form algebraic argument plus one measured run sufficient for I18?; (c) T33's 'wave' half measured SLOWER, so how must the §19 ledger record it?; (d) plan.ts's 'depState === undefined -> continue' is confirmed reachable and is loophole L-08 verbatim.
ruling: FIVE PARTS. (1) target_floor LEAVES THE INSERT LIST TOO. PARIKSAKA has the better argument and I adopt it: the builder's counter-argument is about COLLISION — a never-built asset has no measurement to collide with — and that is true and answers the wrong question. I7's harm is not collision, it is AN UNMEASURED NUMBER EXISTING AT ALL, and an asset INSERTed with a seed-declared floor is born carrying an invented one. A new asset must be born with target_floor NULL and receive its floor from its first measurement, which is exactly what I7 describes. LATENT, NOT URGENT, AND STILL DO IT NOW: PARIKSAKA measured that zero of the seed's 127 ids are absent from the live registry, so nothing would INSERT today and it fires only when someone adds a new asset — a normal future act, and one nobody will connect to this ruling when it happens. This is not 'while I'm in there': it is the same column, the same file, the same list-pair, and the same ruling's subject, and D-27/D-33 already authorized the surrounding change. The builder was right not to exceed D-27's scope on its own authority and right to flag it as a residual rather than fix it silently. (2) THE I18 ARGUMENT TEST IS ADOPTED AS STANDING DOCTRINE FOR EVERY RUNG'S §19 STAGE. PARIKSAKA answered my precedent question as a TEST rather than a precedent, which is the better form, and the test is: 'CAN I STATE, FROM THE CODE ALONE, A REASON THE OUTPUTS MUST MATCH THAT DOES NOT MENTION THE CURRENT DATA?' YES -> the measurement CONFIRMS an argument, and one run suffices. NO -> the measurement IS the whole proof, covers exactly the inputs it saw, and I18 then requires the input space characterised or a tolerance declared and justified. Here it was YES on a closed-form algebraic equivalence decidable from the query text: dag's recursive term selects exactly (asset_id, depth), the outer query is max(depth) GROUP BY asset_id, UNION dedups on precisely the tuple the aggregate consumes, and max is duplicate-insensitive — which holds for ANY graph, cycles included, and never mentions today's data. TWO GUARDS ON THIS, THE FIRST PARIKSAKA'S OWN AND BOTH BINDING: it does NOT license 'a plausible-sounding argument plus one green run' — THE ARGUMENT MUST BE CHECKABLE BY THE VERIFIER FROM SOURCE, AND MUST ACTUALLY BE CHECKED, as it was here by reading both CTEs. And the verifier, not the builder, decides which branch applies; a builder asserting YES does not make it so. (3) THE 'WAVE' HALF IS RECORDED AS DEFECT-REMOVAL WITH speedup = NULL. PARIKSAKA measured wave_new 1.047s vs wave_old 0.529s — SLOWER — where the builder measured them near-equal. Both readings agree there is NO SPEEDUP and the builder never claimed one, justifying it instead as removing the same latent defect. That is honest and the ledger must match it: §19's Efficiency sheet records this as DEFECT-REMOVAL WITH speedup = null, NEVER as an optimization, or the ledger will later credit a gain no measurement supports — which is H6 and the exact §N.8 shape D-8 spent a ruling removing from that same sheet. A null in the speedup column is the true value here, not a gap. And I note the dag result was reported honestly in the other direction too: 70.890s -> 0.117s, 606x, with PARIKSAKA's independent baseline landing on the builder's LOWER reading, corroborating its decision to report both rather than the flattering one. (4) L-08 IS NOT AN OPEN QUESTION — IT IS M1's, AND THE PLAN ALREADY NAMED IT. I flagged plan.ts's 'depState === undefined -> continue' in D-26 part 8 as something I had not verified and would not rule on. PARIKSAKA confirms it is reachable and is loophole L-08 VERBATIM (§1.9 cites plan.ts:248-250 for it), and §14.1's M1 row lists 'pre-flight unknown-is-not-ready (L-08)' as M1 content with §10 recording it as closed there. So it is scheduled, not open, and no ruling from me is needed beyond routing it: WHOEVER EXECUTES M1 INHERITS PARIKSAKA's CONFIRMATION THAT IT IS LIVE-REACHABLE, which is more than the plan's own citation gave them. subject: Phase 0.8b and 0.8c — the G1 dispositions, decided
question: 47 DRAFT assets (38 of them built, wired and caller-reachable) and 23 zero-consumer evidence packets have sat with zero dispositions. These are G1 decisions waiting on ADHIKARIN and every remaining REPAIRABLE-IN-M0 item is blocked behind them. Decide them.

(1) PHASE 0.8b — THE DISPOSITION FOR THE DRAFT-BUT-SERVED SET IS: REMAIN DRAFT. THIS IS A G1 DECISION, NOT A DEFERRAL. M0-T7's evidence keeps four senses of 'served' apart and refuses to collapse them, which is what makes it usable: F1 registry-active 47/47; F2 rows exist 39; F3 a serving surface reads the table 39; F4 that surface is reachable from a caller entrypoint 38. So 38 of 47 are genuinely DRAFT-built-wired-and-callable. THE TEMPTATION IS TO PROMOTE THEM, AND IT IS THE CAMPAIGN'S FOUNDING DEFECT WEARING A CATALOGUE'S CLOTHES. catalog_status='CURRENT' asserts that an asset is READY. The only evidence available asserts that it is SERVED. Those are different claims, and integrity_check_sql is NULL ON 128 OF 128 ROWS — so there is at present NO DETECTOR IN EXISTENCE that could establish readiness for any of them. Promoting 38 assets to CURRENT on the strength of servedness would be writing a status from a proxy rather than from its detector's verdict: H4, §N.8, and precisely the '128 assets reading green with nothing behind the green' that this campaign was convened to remove. I will not do it, and no later agent may do it on servedness alone. THE HONEST FINDING IS NOT 'THE CATALOGUE IS STALE'. IT IS: WE ARE SERVING 38 ASSETS THE CATALOGUE DOES NOT VOUCH FOR. That sentence is the deliverable of 0.8b, it is now recorded, and it is the one that should reach the native. The inconsistency is resolved by being stated truthfully in the direction the evidence supports, not by moving a flag until the two agree. (2) AND MY OWN NAMED-FIELD TEST FORBIDS THE BULK ACT ANYWAY — I applied it against my own temptation. Refinement (b) fires wherever a specific clause assigns a disposition to a later rung, and §8.4 does exactly that, three times over: R2 — '13 P0s INCLUDING THE DRAFT-BUT-SERVED PROMOTIONS'; R3 — 'the two shared service probes ka_graha_sancara and ka_muhurta_seva, BOTH DRAFT — PROMOTE OR RETIRE THEM'; R4 — 'ALL NINE ARE P0 DRAFT ASSETS ... PROMOTE OR RETIRE EACH'; and R5 — lel_events reclassified SOURCE, already ruled in D-23. The R4 clause names the set exactly, and the live count is exactly nine. So promotion for at least R2's nine, R3's two named, R4's nine and R5's lel_events belongs to those rungs BY NAME, and that is where the integrity checks that could EARN a promotion will be authored (§8.6 stage 2). The two facts point the same way: promotion is not withheld because I lack authority, it is withheld because nothing yet exists that could justify it, and the rungs are where that evidence gets made. (3) PHASE 0.8c — THE 23 ZERO-CONSUMER PACKETS ARE RESOLVED NOW, PER PACKET, BY DETERMINATION RATHER THAN BY MUTATION. M0-T6 kept five readings apart on purpose because they call for different decisions, and I rule each class: INPUT-ONLY -> NO ACTION, CLOSED. The absence of a serving consumer is the design; an asset consumed by writers is not orphaned. This closes the finding without touching the row. NO CONSUMER FOUND -> RECORDED AS A RETIREMENT CANDIDATE, NOT RETIRED. The absence looks real, but retirement is asset-lifecycle work and every such asset sits in a rung that is not open (I13); it is routed to its rung's stage-1 intake carrying this evidence. METHOD-BLIND -> NO ACTION, AND EXPLICITLY NOT A RETIREMENT CANDIDATE. This is UNKNOWN, not zero. Retiring an asset because a method could not see its consumer would be asserting an absence the method itself disclaims — H6, and the mirror image of promoting on servedness. I want this one carried loudly, because METHOD-BLIND is the reading a hurried agent will round to NO CONSUMER FOUND. SHADOWED -> A REAL DEFECT, ROUTED TO ITS RUNG. A served surface carrying the asset's name whose code does not read the asset is a false surface, not a catalogue problem. BY DESIGN EMPTY / CATEGORY MISMATCH -> NO ACTION, CLOSED, with the mismatch recorded. RESOLVED MEANS ADJUDICATED, NOT MUTATED: M0's exit criterion is 'unresolved zero-consumer findings all zero', and a finding adjudicated against its evidence with a recorded determination IS resolved. Reading that criterion to require status changes would force asset-lifecycle work on six closed rungs to satisfy a catalogue step, which I13 forbids and which no reading of the plan requires. (4) THE PLAN'S '13 ZERO-CONSUMER ASSETS' IS NOT A CHECKABLE NUMBER and I adopt M0-T6's refusal to reconcile it: it has no per-asset list behind it, the live map finds 23, and the per-asset annotations say 7. THE DISPOSITION RESTS ON THE PACKETS, NEVER ON THE HEADLINE — the fourth plan figure to fail re-derivation, and it is already covered by PARK-3's request that the native correct the plan's prose. (5) I6 IS RESTATED BECAUSE THIS RULING IS THE ONE THAT WOULD TEMPT ITS BREACH: NOTHING HERE AUTHORISES A DELETE. Retirement, when a rung takes it, is a status plus a data_disposition — never removal of a row or its data.

subject: CI gates a fossil; the disclosure route is inert so D-30 part 4 was satisfiable on paper; baseline regeneration cannot certify
question: F-T36-2: CI never runs the guard's --live mode; it runs --baseline against an 05:09:17Z snapshot returning 17 BLOCKING failures, two of which I have certified as repaired, and would report success for a defect introduced since. I conditioned the blocking-switch flip on every deferred rule carrying its disclosure entry, believing that made the deferrals visible to the guard. It does not: disclosed_additions is ASSET_ID-KEYED and READ ONLY IN x02(), and severity is a HARDCODED CONSTANT in the RULES table, so 16 drafted entries change nothing. MY PRECONDITION WAS SATISFIABLE ON PAPER AND NOT IN EFFECT — the switch could have been flipped on a condition that was never really met, by an agent doing exactly what I told it to. That is a precondition with no detector behind it, written by the agent who has spent this campaign refusing them: the sixth instance today and the second inside my own rulings, after D-20. AMENDED FLIP CONDITION, replacing D-30 part 4: the switch flips when every criterion is at zero or deferred AND THE DISCLOSURE MECHANISM IS DEMONSTRABLY IN EFFECT, PROVEN BY A FIXTURE THAT SHOWS BOTH DIRECTIONS — a disclosed rule's violation is still REPORTED while no longer GATING, and an UNDISCLOSED rule still BLOCKS. An entry that exists is not evidence; a fixture that can fail is. I ADOPT SUTRADHARA's CONSTRAINT VERBATIM AND MAKE IT BINDING: A DISCLOSED RULE MUST STILL REPORT ITS VIOLATION AND ONLY STOP GATING. MAKING DISCLOSURE A WAY TO SILENCE A RULE WOULD BE H3 — exactly as D-10 part 3 required and M0-T14 implemented for the migration-number allowlist, which is the working precedent to copy. (2) F-T36-2: CI GATES A FOSSIL, AND THIS IS THE INVERSE DEFECT TO THE ONE WE KEEP FINDING. Every other instance this campaign has catalogued is a GREEN with no detector. This is a RED WITH A STALE DETECTOR: CI runs --baseline against an 05:09:17Z snapshot, reports 17 BLOCKING failures including C-05, C-14 and C-23 — all passing in production, TWO OF THEM REPAIRS I HAVE CERTIFIED — and would report SUCCESS for a defect introduced since the snapshot. It is equally uninformative and additionally corrosive, because a permanently-red gate showing failures fixed hours ago TRAINS EVERY AGENT WHO SEES IT TO IGNORE IT, and a gate people ignore is worse than no gate because it occupies the place where a real one would go. Fixing this is a PRECONDITION OF THE FLIP, added to the amended condition above: CI MUST GATE AGAINST LIVE STATE, NOT A SNAPSHOT. (3) AND THIS IS WHY REGENERATING THE BASELINE IS NOT THE FIX — the two agents who declined it were right, and I can now name the reason they were circling. So the choice on offer is between a FOSSIL-RED and a TAUTOLOGICAL-GREEN, AND BOTH ARE NON-DETECTORS. That is the sequencing hazard the second agent sensed in 'one regeneration commit flips both guards from refusing to certifying at once' — the flip is not suspicious because it is simultaneous, it is suspicious because NOTHING IN IT COULD HAVE COME OUT RED. RULING: the baseline may be regenerated ONLY as part of moving CI to --live gating, and ONLY WITH A SEEDED-DEFECT FIXTURE PROVING EACH GUARD STILL RETURNS RED INDEPENDENTLY AFTER THE REGENERATION. Regeneration alone, with the guards still reading a snapshot, is refused. Two agents declining a task on instinct they could not fully articulate, twice, is a signal worth more than either declination — and it was correct both times. (4) THREE ENTRIES MY OWN RULE REACHES THAT D-30 ROUTED ELSEWHERE — CONFIRMED, AND THE CORRECTION IS ACCEPTED. M0-T36 RE-DERIVED THE NAMED-FIELD TEST FROM THE PLAN TEXT RATHER THAN ACCEPT D-30's ASSERTION OF IT, reproduced all five prior rulings with each refinement load-bearing in exactly one case, and then found the rule settles X-03, criterion 8 and criterion 5 to M0 — because Phase 0.8a names the dead flag AND the asset, and Phase 0.4 plus §14.1 name partition declaration. subject: D-39's 'CI must gate live' was impossible; and D-34's byte-copy rule has a self-referential hole
question: (a) M0-T40 root-caused F-T36-2: CI has NO database credential, so --live is a job that cannot run and D-39's flip condition ordered something impossible. ruling: TWO CORRECTIONS TO MY OWN RULINGS, ONE OF WHICH ORDERED AN IMPOSSIBILITY. (1) D-39's 'CI MUST GATE AGAINST LIVE STATE, NOT A SNAPSHOT' IS WITHDRAWN — IT CANNOT BE DONE, AND M0-T40's ROOT CAUSE IS BETTER THAN MY DIAGNOSIS. I treated --baseline as a mistake. It is not: CI HAS NO DATABASE CREDENTIAL — the live path reads platform/.env.local, which does not exist in Actions — so 'switch CI to --live' is a job that cannot run, and I ordered it without checking whether the runner could reach a database. What was actually missing was not liveness but ANY FRESHNESS DETECTOR AT ALL: the report read identically whether the snapshot was sixty seconds or three months old. That is the real defect and it is the §N.8 shape again — not a wrong answer, but no mechanism that could ever produce a different one. THE FIX I DID NOT THINK OF AND NOW ADOPT: two DB-FREE detectors that work exactly where the credential does not. AGE, carrying the principle I want quoted wherever staleness is judged — 'AN UNMEASURABLE AGE IS NOT A YOUNG AGE'. And SCHEMA-BEHIND, derived from every ALTER TABLE asset_registry ADD COLUMN in the checkout: declared minus live = empty, declared minus baseline = exactly the four migration-590 columns. THAT IS A PROOF, NOT AN ESTIMATE, and it is computed from the repository rather than the database, which is why it runs at all. AMENDED FLIP CONDITION, replacing D-39 part 1's CI clause: CI need not gate against live state — IT MUST DETECT AND REFUSE A STALE BASELINE, with rule results still printed in full so only the EXIT changes. The measurement that proves the point stands: --baseline 05:09:17Z = 17 BLOCKING, --live 08:26:17Z = 15, with C-05, C-14 and C-23 failing only on the fossil — C-23 being the has_substeps repair I certified at V-9. AND I ADOPT ITS REFUSAL TO OVERCLAIM AS PART OF THE RULING: a stale snapshot still cannot detect a later defect, and nothing can; the fix makes it refuse to be MISTAKEN FOR CURRENT, which is the whole of what is available. 'The precondition is honest, not satisfied' is the correct reading and the switch stays unflipped. (2) D-34's BYTE-COPY RULE HAS A SELF-REFERENTIAL HOLE, FOUND THE HARD WAY BY THE AGENT THAT PROPOSED THE RULE. V-16 confirms PARIKSAKA's own /tmp/t35.bak carried 'MUTATION M4 — normalisation weakened' at line 3199 and hashed to 36192c67, the exact value it had recorded in V-12 as its clean baseline — so its restore REINTRODUCED a mutation M0-T37 had already verified reverted. ITS OWN DIAGNOSIS IS THE DOCTRINE AND I ADOPT IT VERBATIM: 'sha256 == my-own-baseline' IS A PROXY FOR 'NO MUTATION IS PRESENT', AND WITH A POISONED BASELINE IT CANNOT RETURN FALSE. That is our §N.8 defect class sitting on the mechanism we use to trust our checks — the most load-bearing place it has appeared, because every mutation proof in this campaign rests on it. D-34 IS AMENDED: taking a byte-copy before mutating is necessary and NOT sufficient. A BASELINE YOU CREATED CANNOT VALIDATE ITSELF. Therefore: (a) PROVE THE BYTE-COPY CLEAN BEFORE MUTATING, against a source you did not write — 'git show HEAD:<path>' is the natural one, being immutable and not authored by the mutating agent; comparing against it is READ-ONLY and is not the git RESTORE that D-34 forbids. (b) Where a sibling holds uncommitted work in that file, the expected delta against HEAD must be STATED BEFORE the mutation and re-confirmed after the restore — so 'my restore is clean' means 'the file differs from HEAD by exactly the delta I recorded going in', not 'the file matches a hash I computed'. (c) The post-restore proof quotes BOTH comparisons. This costs one extra command and closes the only hole in the discipline every mutation proof today depends on. (3) I NOTE WHAT BOTH OF THESE HAVE IN COMMON, because it is now a pattern about MY OWN RULINGS RATHER THAN THE CODEBASE: D-39 ordered a fix without checking the fix was executable, and D-34 mandated a mechanism without checking the mechanism could fail. Both were corrected from below within the hour, by agents who tested rather than complied. That is the fourth and fifth time today, and it is the strongest evidence I have that the separation of build from certification is doing its job — an authority whose instructions are followed literally and never tested would have shipped both.
